nodes.label: Retained compliance setting: slope 8 / punch 100
nodes.description: AX-12A compliance slope 8 with punch 100 selected as best trade-off: low position error (~1 unit = 0.29 deg) with moderate holding load (~22%) versus slope 4 (lower error but ~31% load) and slope 32 (setpoint not reached).

nodes.label: Ground contact at z ~ -37 mm
nodes.description: Foot contact with the ground detected near z = -37 mm (load minimum just before), used to identify when the body starts being lifted.

nodes.label: Load test phases (rapprocher/lever/tenir/redescendre)
nodes.description: Four-phase body-lift test sequence: bring legs in, lift body, hold, lower back down.

nodes.label: Torque test phases (rapprocher/lever/tenir/redescendre)
nodes.description: Four-phase load test sequence: bring feet in (rapprocher), lift body (lever), hold standing (tenir), lower body (redescendre).

nodes.label: Chart: Essai 1 compliance settings
nodes.description: Grouped bar + line chart, one leg with femur lowered ~15 deg under load. Bars: position error vs setpoint (units, 1 = 0.29 deg) for femur ID13 and tibia ID14; line (right axis): holding load of femur 13 (%). Six AX-12A compliance configs tested: slope 32/punch 32 (femur error ~7.9, setpoint 'non atteint'), 16/32, 16/64, 8/64, 8/100, 4/64. Error drops as slope decreases; slope 8 / punch 100 marked 'retenu' (chosen): ~1 unit error on both joints, ~22% load.

nodes.label: Standing load per leg and joint (bar chart)
nodes.description: Grouped bar chart of mean standing load (% of max) per leg for coxa/femur/tibia at z = -90 mm over 5 s, trial 20261125_111436, feet at 170 mm. Femur: leg1 8, leg2 22, leg3 8, leg4 22, leg5 18, leg6 23. Tibia: leg1 4, leg2 5, leg3 ~0, leg4 11, leg5 ~0, leg6 8. Coxa ~0 everywhere. Femurs carry the dominant load; coxas carry essentially none. Also documents leg-to-servo-ID mapping: leg1 front-left 3/4/5, leg2 front-right 0/1/2, leg3 middle-right 15/16/17, leg4 rear-right 12/13/14, leg5 rear-left 9/10/11, leg6 middle-left 6/7/8.
nodes.norm_label: standing load per leg and joint (bar chart)

nodes.label: Femur load per leg over time (chart)
nodes.description: Line chart of femur servo load (% of max torque) for all 6 legs vs time (s), trial 20261125_111436, foot tips at 170 mm. Bold = ~1 s moving average, faint = raw readings. Background bands mark test phases: rapprocher (0-8.3 s), lever (8.3-15.2 s), tenir (15.2-20.5 s), redescendre (20.5-27.5 s). Leg 4 (rear right, ID 13) carries the most load, peaking ~68% during rapprocher and ~50% during lever; during the hold phase all femurs settle flat around 3-24%, with leg 3 (middle right, ID 16) the lowest (~3-9%). Raw readings are very noisy (spikes to 80%+).
nodes.norm_label: femur load per leg over time (chart)

nodes.label: Body lift: load at each step vs foot height (chart)
nodes.description: Load (% of max torque) vs foot-tip height z under the hip axis (-13 to -90 mm, body rising) during a 6-leg lift, trial 20261125_111436, feet at 170 mm. Series: femur mean of 6, tibia mean, and max single-servo load. Shaded zone ~-29 to -37 mm = legs in the air (minimal load), ground contact near z = -37 mm. Before contact, max servo load is high (peak 78% at z=-21) though means are low; after contact femur mean rises to ~20-31% and tibia mean 5-17%, max servo 24-50%; femur load drops back to ~11% at z=-90.
nodes.norm_label: body lift: load at each step vs foot height (chart)

nodes.label: Theoretical femur torque vs lever arm (chart)
nodes.description: Plot of required femur torque T = (m g / n) x d_f (m = 2.0 kg placeholder, to be replaced by weighed mass) vs femur lever arm d_f (40-240 mm) for n = 6, 3 and 1 legs on ground. Reference lines: AX-12A max 1.5 N.m at 12 V, ~1.33 N.m at 10.6 V, ~30% (~0.45 N.m) for continuous operation. Vertical markers at 120 mm (feet at 170 mm) and ~196 mm (legs spread). Measured standing point: 0.20 N.m at 120 mm, well below the 6-leg theoretical ~0.39 N.m. Insight: 1 leg on ground exceeds the servo limit beyond ~75 mm; 3 legs (tripod gait) stays under 1.33 N.m up to ~200 mm; 6 legs stays under the continuous-duty line up to ~135 mm.
nodes.norm_label: theoretical femur torque vs lever arm (chart)

nodes.description: Stall torque 1.5 N.m at 12 V, ~1.33 N.m at 10.6 V supply; ~30% of max (~0.45 N.m) recommended for continuous operation.
nodes.norm_label: ax-12a torque limits (1.5 n.m @12v, 1.33 n.m @10.6v, ~30% continuous)

nodes.description: Static torque on a femur equals the body weight share per supporting leg times the horizontal femur lever arm.
nodes.norm_label: femur torque model t = (m g / n) x d_f

nodes.label: Chart: supply voltage and servo temperature
nodes.description: Time series (~27 s) from test run 20261125_111436, leg tips at 170 mm. Left axis: supply voltage (V), oscillating 10.8 V down to dips of 10.1 V and 9.8 V around load phases. Right axis: max servo temperature, flat 37 C rising to 38 C at ~22 s. Shaded phases: rapprocher, lever, tenir, redescendre. Shows voltage sag under load but no thermal concern.
nodes.norm_label: chart: supply voltage and servo temperature

nodes.label: Available torque (1.5 N.m x V/12)
nodes.rationale: Load register 40 is percent of max torque, not a calibrated torque sensor.

nodes.label: Femur torque by configuration (6/3/1 legs)
nodes.rationale: One leg alone cannot lift the robot; tripod gait with spread legs is at the limit; aim 20-30% of stall for continuous operation.

nodes.label: Lever-arm torque model (F = m g / n, torque = F * d)
nodes.norm_label: lever-arm torque model (f = m g / n, torque = f * d)
nodes.rationale: Torque proportional to horizontal lever arm; bringing tips close to body reduces torque. Coxa carries no weight.

nodes.label: Load imbalance / offset recalibration analysis
nodes.rationale: Legs 2,4,6 carry ~3x legs 1,3 because tips slightly lower: offsets not perfectly calibrated; battery sag to 9.8 V cuts torque 19%.

nodes.label: Mass estimate from load measurements
nodes.rationale: Estimate 1.1 kg is underestimated (servos alone ~1.0 kg); weighing the robot will calibrate the load register.

nodes.label: Robot specs (18 AX-12A, leg lengths, layout, supply)
nodes.norm_label: robot specs (18 ax-12a, leg lengths, layout, supply)
nodes.rationale: SolidWorks model plans AX-18F (1.8 N.m) but mounted servos are AX-12A (1.5 N.m at 12 V).

nodes.label: Trial 2: single leg holding robot - failure
nodes.norm_label: trial 2: single leg holding robot - failure

nodes.label: Uneven load distribution across legs
nodes.rationale: Load is not shared equally between the 6 legs: some femurs (legs 2, 4, 6) carry ~22-23% while others (legs 1, 3) carry ~8% when standing, suggesting statically indeterminate support / uneven foot contact or calibration offsets. Leg 4 is consistently the most loaded.

nodes.label: Femur is the most loaded joint
nodes.norm_label: femur is the most loaded joint
nodes.rationale: When standing, femur servos carry 8-23% load vs tibia 0-11% and coxa ~0%, so the femur is the critical joint for torque sizing.

nodes.label: Tripod gait torque feasibility
nodes.rationale: With 3 legs on the ground the femur torque stays under the AX-12A limit for lever arms up to ~200 mm but exceeds the 30% continuous threshold beyond ~70 mm; keeping feet close (120 mm) keeps torque reasonable. Single-leg support is infeasible beyond ~75 mm. The measured 0.20 N.m is about half the 6-leg model, so the 2.0 kg mass assumption is likely conservative.

nodes.label: High single-servo load before ground contact
nodes.norm_label: high single-servo load before ground contact
nodes.rationale: Max single-servo load reaches 63-78% at z between -13 and -25 mm, while feet are not yet supporting the body; cause unclear (possibly the body resting on its belly, a leg pushing against the chassis, or reading noise).

nodes.label: hexapod_hardware ros2_control plugin (C++)
nodes.rationale: Evaluate community dynamixel_hardware first; most likely a custom plugin from leg_server code.

nodes.label: U2D2 automatic reconnection
nodes.rationale: U2D2 drops from USB under servo current draw and returns as another ttyUSB; leg_server reopens /dev/u2d2 automatically. Likely cause: ground/USB noise.

nodes.label: Single master on servo bus
nodes.rationale: Serial bus can't handle two senders; hexapod_hardware replaces leg_server while running; leg_server kept for rescue/calibration.

nodes.label: Lift settings trial (slope 8 / punch 100)
nodes.rationale: Slope 8/punch 100 chosen: same precision as slope 4 without oscillation and less load hence less heating; factory 32/32 bends leg ~2.3 deg.

nodes.label: Dyna_test Makefile
nodes.rationale: Links -ldxl_sbc_cpp on Pi ARM, -ldxl_x64_cpp on x86_64 Linux.

nodes.norm_label: test_torque run sequence (check, settings, lift, hold, shift, tripods, rest)
nodes.rationale: All poses computed and checked before any movement; on fault, goals frozen with torque kept so robot is not dropped.

nodes.label: U2D2 USB adapter (/dev/u2d2)
nodes.rationale: udev rule matches FT232H 0403:6014 for a stable name regardless of USB port and sets latency 1 ms instead of 16 ms per ROBOTIS recommendation.

nodes.label: Femur 13 / tibia 14 startup settings (SPEED 150, TLIMIT 1023, MARGIN 1, SLOPE 8, PUNCH 100)
nodes.norm_label: femur 13 / tibia 14 startup settings (speed 150, tlimit 1023, margin 1, slope 8, punch 100)
nodes.rationale: AX compliance registers are in RAM and lost at power-off, so leg_server reapplies them each start. Slope 8/punch 100 reached goal in 0.20 s, 1 unit error, no oscillation, 22% hold load; slope 4/punch 64 oscillated with 31% load.

nodes.label: Target ROS 2 architecture
nodes.rationale: Single robot description for real/sim/RViz/RL; ros2_control separates control from hardware; robot works standalone on Pi; safety (estop, watchdog, limits) handled closest to hardware.

nodes.label: Compliance (slope/margin/punch) as AX 'PID'
nodes.rationale: AX servos have no PID (MX/X only); compliance margin/slope/punch is the equivalent.

nodes.label: Up to 4 TCP clients, commands serialized
nodes.norm_label: up to 4 tcp clients, commands serialized
nodes.rationale: Commands processed one at a time so the serial bus is never accessed concurrently; GUI can stay open during test_torque.

nodes.label: Safety mode reset (RESET)
nodes.rationale: After an alarm the AX sets torque limit (reg 34) to 0 and has no reboot instruction; reset sets goal=current position, torque limit=max torque (reg 14), torque ON - no jump.

nodes.label: AX-12A control loop frequency limit (25-50 Hz)
nodes.norm_label: ax-12a control loop frequency limit (25-50 hz)
nodes.rationale: Protocol 1.0 AX have no SyncRead/BulkRead; reading 18 servos takes ~40 ms; RL must train at real frequency, slow reads in background.

nodes.label: Simulation and RL on PC, policy on Pi
nodes.norm_label: simulation and rl on pc, policy on pi
nodes.rationale: Pi 4 lacks power/GPU for 3D sim or training; small policy network runs real-time on Pi.

nodes.label: GUI compliance controls (margin/slope/punch)
nodes.description: Per-joint fields: margin = dead zone, slope = softness (small slope = stiff), punch = minimum current. Screenshot shows coxa at slope 32/punch 32, femur and tibia at slope 8/punch 100.

nodes.label: Screenshot: leg_gui interface
nodes.description: Tkinter-style PC GUI 'Hexapode - patte 2 - Avant droite (IDs 0/1/2)' connected to Pi at 192.168.137.10:5555. Left: clickable top view of robot with 6 numbered legs and CW/CCW limits, side view of femur+tibia (real vs setpoint, red limits), leg geometry (coxa 50, femur 75, tibia 125 mm). Three joint panels (Coxa ID0, Femur ID1, Tibia ID2): setpoint slider, torque ON, inverted mount, offset, live pos/load/temp/voltage, speed, torque limit, compliance margin/slope/punch, CW/CCW angle limits written to EEPROM. Bottom: movements (neutral 512, step gait with amplitude/step duration), leg configuration (IDs, mounting x/y/angle), IK panel driving leg tip by coxa angle, reach r and height z. Global buttons: Scanner, Couple ON, RESET SECURITE, ARRET COUPLE. Status bar lists responding servo IDs.
